fatalSameProcessLockdown.summary: A fatal rollback already kept its journal and its write lock. The running API did not act on it: the read-only flag was startupRecovery.readOnly, a boot-time const, so the same process still believed it could write and the next POST was stopped only by the lock, after a second transaction had started, and reported as a 409 conflict.
changes: RepositoryHealth: one mutable readOnly/reason/fatalTransactionId per process, seeded from startup recovery
markRepositoryFatal is called by the transaction adapter, not by routes, so no write endpoint can report fatal without the process going read-only
the flip is one-way; only a human plus the next startup recovery can clear it
TransactionResult carries the engine state through; transactionStatus maps fatal to 503, not 409
the read-only middleware reads live health per request, refusing writes before a route runs or a transaction directory exists
the 503 body and GET /api/health both name the fatal transaction id and reason
route construction moved from server.ts into createApp so the middleware is testable without binding a port

defectFound.defect: transaction ids were derived from the first path segment of every file under .chamber-transactions/, so write.lock was treated as a journal-less transaction directory and removed by recovery
defectFound.impact: the next startup after a fatal transaction deleted the write lock that transaction was holding
defectFound.fix: only nested paths name a transaction; a restart test asserts the lock survives recovery
